title: Зависть поваров и совет Максу  (The Cooks' Envy and a Tip for Max)

segments.t: After tasting the salad, Senya, Fedya, and Lyova grumble amongst themselves that the young newcomer must have had a rich father help him climb the ladder. Meanwhile, Aleksandr wins Max over by showing him a simple trick to rest meat for two minutes so it cooks much faster.
Ну, я надеюсь, по крайней мере.
Погоди, ты же в метрополе начинал.
После этого ты приготовишь его гораздо быстрее.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'This should be delicious.' Adding that this should be delicious fills in the missing piece for Lyova.
Ну, я надеюсь, по крайней мере.
'Well, I hope so, at least.' Lyova explains that he hopes so at least, keeping his voice calm and direct.
'Or else his daddy helped him out.' Since else his daddy helped him out, Barinov does not waste words on excuses.
'Just like him.' Between the room and the meat, Lyova gives Barinov a quick, grounded response.
'Would have achieved something too.' Barinov reminds Lyova that would have achieved something before the moment passes.

'I would like to see him try.' Because he would like to see him try, Lyova treats the matter as settled. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
'Where I started out.' Explaining that where he started out lays the cards on the table for Lyova.
Погоди, ты же в метрополе начинал.

'Hold on, you started out at the Metropol.' Holding on Barinov started out at the Metropol is how Lyova lays out the situation for Barinov. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.

'Oh, right, it was Lyova who started at the Metropol.' Claiming that right it was Lyova who started at the Metropol sounds confident, even if Lyova has doubts. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
'In order to do that.' Pointing out that in order to do gives Barinov a sobering reality check.
'Beforehand.' Around the meat and shift, Barinov sets a calm, everyday tone with Lyova.
'Let it rest for two minutes.' Since Barinov should let it rest for two minutes, Lyova does not waste words on excuses.
После этого ты приготовишь его гораздо быстрее.

'After that, you will cook it much faster.' Noting that after that Lyova will cook it much faster keeps Barinov's side of the story simple and clear. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Ну, я надеюсь, по крайней мере.
Погоди, ты же в метрополе начинал.
После этого ты приготовишь его гораздо быстрее.
That wraps up this scene as while Senya, Fedya, and Lyova grumble that Aleksandr only got ahead through connections, the new chef wins Max over with a helpful cooking tip. Until next time!
